claims: A home mortgage loan is a secured loan used to purchase property, with the home serving as collateral.
Common types of home mortgage loans include 30-year fixed-rate mortgages.
Common types of home mortgage loans include government-backed loans (FHA, VA, USDA).
Government-backed loans (FHA, VA, USDA) offer lower down payments.
Fixed-Rate Mortgages have interest rates that remain the same for the life of the loan.
Adjustable-Rate Mortgages (ARM) have rates that may change after an initial period.
FHA Loans are insured by the Federal Housing Administration.
FHA Loans allow down payments as low as 3.5%.
VA Loans are for veterans/eligible service members.
VA Loans often have $0 down payment.
USDA Loans are for rural homebuyers with low-to-moderate incomes.
20% down payment is standard to avoid private mortgage insurance (PMI).
As of March 2026, 30-year fixed rates are averaging around 6.16% to 6.375%.
Closing costs include appraisal, attorney fees, and title insurance.
Monthly payment generally includes principal, interest, taxes, and insurance (PITI).
